sentences.text: HC-KAR CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM
ORAL ORDER (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM)

The captioned petition is filed by the accused Nos. 1 to 6 seeking quashing of the proceedings pending in C.C.No.888/2024 for the offences punishable under Sections 143, 147, 323, 354, 504, 506 read with Section 149 of IPC arising out of Crime No.130/2024 of Manvi Police Station.
2.

The gist of the prosecution case, as could be gathered from the complaint and charge sheet materials, is that the complainant is employed as a cook in a hotel and her husband one Mohd. Shafi was a lorry driver.
The couple had six children.

It is alleged that since the complainant's husband was obese, accused Nos.1 and 2-- Ambika and Kalyani respectively advised the complainant to persuade her husband to consume certain health- NC: 2025:KHC-K:7448 HC-KAR oriented nutrition products marketed by Herbalife Nutrition Company.
3. The complainant, acting on this advice, suggested to her husband to try the said herbal products.

Although the complainant's husband is stated to have initially shown reluctance, accused Nos.1 to 3 allegedly prevailed upon the complainant and her husband by representing that several consumers had derived substantial health benefits from the use of such products.
4. It is further alleged that believing the assurances of accused Nos.1 to 3, the complainant and her husband attended a demonstration of the products and thereafter purchased items worth Rs.7,000/-.
The deceased thereafter consumed the said products for one month, reportedly resulting in a weight loss of 4 kilograms.
According to the complainant, accused No.3 again compelled the husband of the complainant to purchase a fresh set of herbal products for the subsequent NC: 2025:KHC-K:7448 HC-KAR month.

It is alleged that upon continued consumption,
the deceased began experiencing stomach pain, back pain, and giddiness.
As his symptoms aggravated, the complainant claims to have taken her husband to various doctors for treatment.
Ultimately, when they visited the Raichur Institute of Medical Sciences, they were informed that the deceased had suffered complete renal failure.

5. The complaint further narrates that on 16.05.2024 at about 1:00 p.m., the complainant, her husband, and two other persons, Javed Khan and Ajmat Khan, went to the footwear shop of accused No.3 located at Basaveshwar Complex, Manvi, and confronted the accused stating that the herbal products supplied by them had allegedly caused kidney failure in the complainant's husband.

It is Ambika vs The State Of Karnataka on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11206542/
3 alleged that at this juncture, accused Nos.1 to 6 formed an unlawful assembly.

sentences.text: Accused Nos.2 and 3 are alleged to have attempted to outrage the modesty of the complainant, while accused No.4/Prema Bai allegedly assaulted her with hands.
When Javed Khan and Ajmat NC: 2025:KHC-K:7448 HC-KAR Khan intervened, accused Nos.5 and 6 allegedly assaulted them as well.
It is further alleged that all accused persons hurled filthy abuses at the complainant and her husband and threatened them with dire consequences.

Based on these allegations, Crime No.130/2024 was registered for offences under Sections 143, 147, 323, 354, 504, 506 read with Section 149 of IPC.
6.

Learned counsel for the petitioners, reiterating the grounds urged in the petition, contends that the continuation of criminal proceedings against the petitioners would amount to abuse of the process of law.

He draws attention to the test reports obtained by the Investigating Officer which form part of the charge sheet and submits that the herbal products in question satisfy the standards prescribed for "Energy Drinks Mixed Powder" under the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The reports, according to him, clearly establish that the products are not harmful.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7448 HC-KAR 7.
He further refers to the OPD records of the Raichur Institute of Medical Sciences relating to the deceased and submits that the deceased was a chronic alcoholic and smoker.

By placing reliance on these medical records, counsel would submit that the complainant, out of frustration caused by her husband's medical condition, has attempted to rope in the petitioners though the renal failure was clearly attributable to the deceased's lifestyle vices.
He thus submits that even if the charge sheet materials are accepted in totality, no offence is made out against the petitioners and therefore, the proceedings deserve to be quashed.

8. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader, placing reliance on the complaint and statements collected during investigation, contends that there are credible allegations that the petitioners assaulted the complainant, abused her, and attempted to outrage her modesty.

Therefore, according to him, the matter requires NC: 2025:KHC-K:7448 HC-KAR to proceed to trial and no interference is warranted at this stage.
9.
I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties and have carefully perused the complaint, charge sheet, medical records, and other materials on record.

10. This Court cannot remain oblivious to the increasing trend among citizens of invoking the criminal justice machinery as a means of venting personal frustration or grievance without adequate foundation.

On a closer scrutiny of the materials on record, it becomes evident that the complainant approached the accused persons in the hope that the herbal products marketed by them would assist her husband in reducing weight.
In the complaint itself, the complainant acknowledges that her husband lost 4 kilograms after consuming the products for one month.

sentences.text: The filing of the present complaint appears to be an offshoot of the unfortunate disclosure made by the doctors at Raichur Institute of Medical Sciences that the complainant's husband had suffered complete renal failure.
The materials placed on record, including medical records, clearly demonstrate that the deceased was a chronic alcoholic and a regular smoker, apart from being obese.
The medical noting unmistakably suggest that the deceased's renal condition was precipitated by his lifestyle addictions rather than the consumption of herbal nutrition products.

12. In this backdrop, the allegations that accused persons assaulted and outraged the modesty of the complainant appear to be a reactionary step, stemming from the complainant's emotional distress and misunderstanding regarding the cause of her husband's ailment.

The chain of events as narrated by the complainant suggests that the confrontation at the shop of accused No.3 was triggered by the complainant's - 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7448 HC-KAR assumption that the petitioners were responsible for her husband's renal failure.

13. Upon an overall evaluation of the charge sheet materials, it is clear that although a verbal altercation may indeed have occurred between the parties, the allegations at their highest attract only minor offences such as those under Sections 323, 504, and 506 of IPC.
The complainant herself admits that she voluntarily approached the accused persons, purchased the products, and initiated their use with the hope of improving her husband's health.

Merely because her expectations were not met, she could not have launched criminal proceedings alleging assault and outraging of modesty, especially when the Investigating Officer has himself collected medical records establishing the deceased's pre-existing conditions.

14. This Court is of the considered view that the present prosecution, culminating in filing of a charge sheet, has subjected the petitioners to undue hardship and - 11 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7448 HC-KAR a prolonged ordeal.
The petitioners, acting with bona fide intention, appear to have merely facilitated the complainant in procuring herbal nutrition products.

Selling such products, in the absence of any illegality or harm established by medical evidence,
cannot render them criminally liable.
The medical evidence unmistakably points to renal failure caused by the deceased's long-standing lifestyle vices.
In such circumstances, allowing the criminal proceedings to continue would amount to permitting abuse of the process of law.

Therefore,
interference under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is warranted.

- 12 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7448 HC-KAR 147, 323, 354, 504, 506 read with Section 149 IPC, are hereby quashed insofar as the petitioners are concerned.
